claims.claim_text: Revolutionary springs throughout history teach that momentary ruptures do not, on their own, ready the working class to seize control of their lives and their futures.
Without disciplined political organization, even the most ambitious movements buckle under the weight of repression.
Springs of Revolution argues that political movements must build resilience to endure.
Springs of Revolution does most of its work in quiet moments between ruptures, building from below and neighbor to neighbor.

Springs of Revolution's R-22 resolution builds on the electoral standards of the Anti-Zionist Resolution introduced by Ahmed H. and passed by the 2023-2025 National Political Committee and over 56 DSA chapters.
Springs of Revolution presents its R-22 resolution as continuing to provide a material counterweight to the Zionist lobby.
Springs of Revolution's R-22 resolution proposes expanding the Stop Fueling Genocide, No Appetite for Apartheid, and Mask Off Maersk campaigns.
Springs of Revolution's R-22 resolution proposes establishing an Arms Embargo Steering Committee to coordinate labor, legislative, and community organizing to disrupt weapons flows to Israel.
Springs of Revolution's R-22 resolution proposes supporting chapters pursuing divestment through pressure campaigns and ballot initiatives.
Springs of Revolution's R-22 resolution proposes developing strategies to protect the movement and build resilience against state repression.
